papers.titleEn: Molecular Conformational Matching Enables Robust Buried Interfaces in Efficient and Temperature-Cycling-Resilient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Temperature fluctuations can disrupt the organization of buried self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs), weaken interfacial contact, and accelerate device degradation. Here, we develop a co‐assembly strategy by incorporating two bisphosphonic acid molecules with distinct linker structures, denoted S1 and S2, into the widely used carbazole‐based SAM [4‐(3,6‐dimethoxy‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl] phosphonic acid (MeO‐4PACz). Compared with S1, S2 exhibits improved conformational compatibility with MeO‐4PACz. The S2/MeO‐4PACz pair also features stronger hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. In addition, S2 possesses a larger molecular dipole and adsorbs more favorably on indium tin oxide. These molecular attributes promote more continuous and spatially uniform coverage. They also strengthen substrate anchoring and homogenize the interfacial potential distribution. The resulting S2‐based co‐assembled SAM (Co‐SAM) provides favorable energy‐level alignment, facilitates hole extraction, and suppresses nonradiative recombination. It also reinforces the buried interface against cyclic thermal stress. Residual stress accumulation is alleviated, interfacial morphology is preserved, and perovskite phase degradation is retarded. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on the S2 Co‐SAM achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.01% and retain 92.8% of their initial efficiency after 500 temperature cycles between −40°C and 85°C. Synergistic molecular and interfacial regulation enables efficient and temperature‐resilient inverted PSCs.
papers.filename: Hairui Liu, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Molecular Conformational Matching Enables Robust Buried Interfaces in Efficient and Temperature-Cycling-Resilient Inverted Perovskite Solar Ce

papers.titleEn: Hydroxyl-Rich Sodium Gluconate Enables Dense SAM Assembly and Enhances Conductivity in NiO x -Based Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel oxide (NiO x )/self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) composite hole transport layers represent a promising configuration for inverted perovskite solar cells (IPSCs). Nevertheless, the insufficient electrical conductivity of NiO x and the limited number of binding sites on its surface lead to incomplete monolayer coverage, resulting in substantial interfacial charge losses that constrain efficiency improvements. To address these issues, we introduce hydroxyl‑rich sodium gluconate (SG) into the NiO x solution. Gluconate anions from SG modulate the electronic properties of NiO x , thereby enhancing its conductivity. Meanwhile, the abundant hydroxyl groups along the SG backbone furnish additional hydrogen‐bonding sites for the subsequent adsorption of the SAM, promoting the formation of a compact and well‐ordered interfacial molecular layer. This dense SAM not only suppresses leakage currents but also optimizes the energetic cascade at the heterojunction, ultimately enabling the resulting IPSCs to achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.24%. During maximum‐power‐point operation under ISOS‑L‑1 protocol, the optimized device preserves 91.6% of the starting output after 1000 h. This work establishes a versatile interfacial engineering approach that overcomes limitations in both SAM assembly and charge transport, offering new opportunities for the development of highly efficient and durable IPSCs.
papers.filename: Xuanhua Li, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Hydroxyl-Rich Sodium Gluconate Enables Dense SAM Assembly and Enhances Conductivity in NiO x -Based Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Cas12a Autocatalytic Amplification Coupled with a DNA-Regulated COF Nanozyme Activation for the Colorimetric Detection of Staphylococcus aureus
papers.abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) is a major foodborne and clinical pathogen, and its rapid and accurate detection are essential for food safety monitoring and clinical diagnostics. Here, we developed a colorimetric platform for quantifying S. aureus that integrates circular DNA (Cir-DNA)-mediated Cas12a autocatalytic amplification with DNA regulation of a covalent organic framework (COFTph-BT) nanozyme. Recognition of the 16S rDNA target by the Cas12a/crRNA complex activates trans-cleavage activity, which linearizes Cir-DNA and initiates an autocatalytic amplification circuit that drives cascade cleavage of probe S1. Signal transduction exploits the differential binding affinities of COFTph-BT for single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) and double-stranded DNA (dsDNA), and its peroxidase activities could be reversely regulated by the surface modification of ssDNA. Cleavage of S1 inhibits its hybridization with COFTph-BT surface-bound S2, maintaining S2 predominantly in its single-stranded form and preserving the catalytic activity of COFTph-BT-S2. The nanozyme subsequently catalyzes the oxidation of colorless 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) to blue oxidized TMB (oxTMB), generating a colorimetric readout. The assay can be completed within 90 min and achieves a limit of detection (LOD) of 7 CFU mL−1. Integration with smartphone-based image analysis further enables portable colorimetric detection with an LOD of 87 CFU mL−1. This strategy provides an approach for the sensitive colorimetric detection of foodborne pathogens, with potential applications in food safety monitoring and clinical diagnostics.
papers.filename: Deshuai Zhen, Anal. Chem., 2026, Cas12a Autocatalytic Amplification Coupled with a DNA-Regulated COF Nanozyme Activation for the Colorimetric Detection of Staphylococcus aureus

papers.titleEn: Portable Photoactivated Room-Temperature Gas Sensor for On-Site Methanol Monitoring
papers.abstract: Methanol is an essential chemical feedstock and renewable fuel, yet its high volatility and flammability necessitate intrinsically safe room-temperature detection for safe deployment. Current room-temperature methanol sensing technologies, however, suffer from inadequate sensitivity and high detection limits, hindering reliable early leakage warning. Herein, we report a photoactivated room-temperature, chemiresistive methanol sensor based on bimetallic PdPt clusters-decorated W18O49. Bimetallic PdPt clusters with tunable compositions dramatically improve the sensor receptor function via selectively increasing the adsorption of chemisorbed oxygen species and methanol molecules, as revealed by theoretical calculations. Meanwhile, ultraviolet (UV) photoactivation replaces thermal activation by promoting charge-carrier generation and surface redox reactions, while the Schottky barrier enables efficient charge-carrier separation, thereby enhancing the sensor transducer function. The enhanced sensing reaction pathway is elucidated by in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) under UV irradiation. Accordingly, the sensor exhibits a more than fourfold enhancement in response, low detection limit (100 ppb), and stable operation for over 30 days in ambient air at room temperature. Finally, we integrate the sensor into a portable on-site monitoring device, providing an intrinsically safe platform for real-time methanol leakage monitoring and early warning in hazardous industrial environments.
papers.filename: Peng Sun, ACS Sens., 2026, Portable Photoactivated Room-Temperature Gas Sensor for On-Site Methanol Monitoring

papers.titleEn: Non-local Molecular Engineering Modulates Aluminum-Induced Crystallization toward Transferable Polycrystalline Silicon
papers.abstract: Abstract Low-temperature metal-induced crystallization (MIC) has emerged as a promising and cost-effective technique for fabricating polycrystalline silicon (poly-Si), which is a key material in high-performance flexible electronics. However, conventional MIC often yields structurally compromised films due to chaotic interfacial thermodynamics and incomplete layer exchange. Herein, a molecular-level engineering strategy is presented that utilizes buried self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) to remotely control the macroscopic phase transformation and crystallization kinetics during MIC with aluminum as the metal. By systematically tailoring the terminal functional groups of the SAMs at the buried interface between the Al/Si stack and substrate (glass), a distinct structure-property relationship is established: electron-withdrawing groups intrinsically stabilize the amorphous Si (a-Si) network and suppress segregation, whereas electron-donating groups facilitate silicon dissolution. Notably, the best-performing SAM with nucleophilic –NH2 terminal groups functions as a dual-role molecular template that drastically lowers the macroscopic crystallization barrier of the MIC system. By driving a highly directed and accelerated kinetic pathway, this monolayer substantially suppresses stochastic interdiffusion, yielding a highly segregated, continuous, and transfer-ready poly-Si film. Ultimately, this SAM-mediated paradigm advances the fundamental design of non-local phase transformations, establishing a scalable, material-driven pathway for next-generation flexible silicon electronics.
papers.filename: Yian Tai, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Non-local Molecular Engineering Modulates Aluminum-Induced Crystallization toward Transferable Polycrystalline Silicon
